title: Order to Assassinate the King
text: “So that’s apparently what happened.”
Listening to Rafumi’s report—delivered to us the next afternoon when she found a spare moment—Father pressed a hand to his brow and groaned as if utterly exasperated.

“Those high-and-mighty human beings never change, do they. Doing something to a member of the royal family who’d become inconvenient for them… taking over the castle and issuing a false order in Ren-san’s name? And I suppose the ‘impostor’ who fled must have been the real one.”
“And here I wanted to quit playing body double as soon as possible, and now this!”
“How unfortunate. Just when you were trying to arrange for the real king’s return, an order came down to assassinate both Naofumi-san and King Aultcray.”
Ren, back in his human form, groaned in frustration.
“Like hell I’m putting up with an order like that! I’m heading to another country—”
“You’re basically already living there in hiding, though.”
“…I can’t just ignore Princess Melty!”
Ren’s attempt at bravado was spinning its wheels, I say.
“Ah, he corrected himself right away… well, you did live together for a little while, after all.”

Incidentally, I was currently, for some reason, done up as an usaunny and hung upside down in a rolled-up mat as punishment. Not as part of any contest, mind you—Father apparently wanted me strung up like this as a sort of performance to vent Itsuki and the others’ pent-up frustration. Every so often Itsuki fired an arrow at me, but I caught every single one, indeed. Still, each time, I swayed—plip, plop—with the impact.
“Nano! Making keychains like this would be good, nano!”
Hey! Rival, stop poking me, I say-pyon!
“Is Filo-tan safe!?”

I simply could not believe that Filo-tan might have been killed, caught up in some conspiracy. If anyone had truly done such a thing, I would blast the entire Melromarc castle to smithereens, I say. No—I would make the culprit suffer the same wretched fate as Takt, indeed.
“That part’s fine—Filo’s still giving off a response, so I think she got away safely.”

What a relief, I say. Filo-tan was safe. Besides, even if someone had tried something like that, Filo-tan had been raised properly by Father, so she ought to be strong. At the very least, she wouldn’t fall behind mere Melromarc soldiers.
“Rafumi and the others who were in the castle probably would have noticed something at the time of the incident, right? What happened there?”

“Ah, as it happens, the soldiers had called us out to the training grounds right around then, wanting to hear tales of the Hero’s valor, and made us give a whole lecture. On top of that, they’d apparently sealed off the sound with magic quite thoroughly, so as to keep the incident from being noticed.”

“Wow, thorough… I guess even if the king wanted to join up with you all, with that many soldiers around, an all-out clash was unavoidable, so he reluctantly gave up on reuniting with Rafumi and the rest of Ren’s group.”
“If Princess Melty and the others were told that prioritizing escape was necessary, there’s a good chance they’d have gone along with it.”
“Either way… that’s a pretty bold move. Or, wait—since he got away, did they just fabricate some crime and stage an explosion at the castle to cover it up?”
Quite plausible, I say. A thoroughly clichéd conspiracy, indeed.
“How did the king manage to escape with everyone, though? Wasn’t he the Staff Hero or something? Did he use the staff’s teleport skill to get away somewhere?”
“No, I doubt the current king has a weapon that responds to him anymore. Most likely, he used one of the emergency escape passages inside the castle and fled through the underground waterway.”
The Melromarc escape route, I say. Even though it’s a bit of a cliché, this was the first time I’d actually heard of it being used properly for its intended purpose.
“So… Rafumi, who’s playing Ren’s body double, was ordered to track them down—did she manage to find out where the king and the others are hiding?”
Father asked Rafumi with an easy, relaxed air.
“Like I’d ever tell you! Is what this guy would say.”

“Heh… I’m not quite so tactless as that. That said, might this not prove a valuable experience for that king? With that in mind, I’ve quietly slipped in one of my clones as an escort, keeping watch over them from nearby without making it obvious.”
“You’ve got it completely under control, then!”
“Guess we don’t need to get too involved after all…”
Both Itsuki and Ren adopted an attitude of ‘not my problem,’ indeed.
“Will the king and the others be all right after escaping the castle?”

“It’s only been a day since they fled, hasn’t it? Filo did a fine job of running them ragged and shaking off their pursuers plenty well. We can just reunite with them later and lord it over them a bit.”
“Well… I guess that’s true. But if that king fled the castle, does that mean he’s starting to think about reconciling with me?”
Who could say? Back during the loop when Tiger Girl had been handed over early on, no reconciliation with Father had ever come of it.
“Still difficult, I’d wager. I imagine he’s acting purely out of attachment to Tiger Girl, and nothing more, I say.”
“Somehow that feels like it could be its own kind of trouble.”
“There’s never been a case of reconciliation understood without a corresponding sacrifice, I say.”

Just as in the first world, where the queen had passed away, or some incident had to occur that confirmed the Crimson Swine as the true source of his grudge—something along those lines seemed necessary. As for the Crimson Swine in this loop, I had no intention of simply killing her off quickly; I intended to make her suffer, little by little, an agony rivaling what Takt went through. And yet, wherever she was currently wandering off to… well, it was surely only a matter of time before she was caught. Every path she might take had already been sealed off. In fact, subjecting the Pig King to prolonged torment—neither letting him live comfortably nor granting him death—might well be the way to go. I already had a plan set for dealing with the Crimson Swine, but as for Trash, I was still torn over what the best resolution might be. When it came to Tiger Girl, I wanted to avoid anything too cruel myself, after all…
“Either way, we ought to lend a hand before any truly fatal damage occurs… it’s also a problem letting the Three Heroes Church keep exploiting Melromarc as they please.”

“Indeed, that’s certainly true. It’s not exactly game knowledge, but there’s a lot to be gained from dealing with the troublemakers… Perhaps storming the castle and wiping them all out would be best.”
“Itsuki… that’s exactly the kind of thing Motoyasu-kun would say.”

“What an infuriating thing to say. Fine then, in that case, we should simply go about it openly, backed by the authority of someone with real power. The queen is the rightful ruler, isn’t she? If we return triumphantly alongside her and mete out justice to those occupying the castle, wouldn’t that give us proper legitimacy?”

“That does seem like the safest bet… persuading the king, or rather, moving things forward without clashing with me, more or less requires it. Besides, she’s the person Eclair-san’s been wanting to meet, isn’t she—— shouldn’t she be getting back into the area around now?”
“Indeed, the timing does seem about right, I say.”

And so our course of action was decided. As the queen prepared to make her triumphant return, arrangements were quietly made through Faubrey and Siltvelt for a reunion. However, Father and the others refused to let me go anywhere near Trash, Fiancée, or Filo-tan.
And so, while we waited… Fleon-chan grew up splendidly, I say!
“Fleon-chan has grown up, so allow me to make the introduction, I say!”
Recently, at Zeltoble, which had become our base of operations, I proudly unveiled Fleon-chan—who had properly transformed into her angelic form—before everyone!
“I’m Fleon!”

Of course, everyone had been watching her since she was a chick. Since I’d done my best to keep her diet and growth timeline as faithful to the original as possible, I believe she turned out quite similarly. Fleon-chan went pata-pata, flying about on the wings on her back.
“Ooh.”
“She’s flying—”
“Lucky—”
“Does she get put somewhere prominent when we sing and dance at the circus?”
The various Filolial-samas offered their thoughts, each watching Fleon-chan fly.

“Per the wishes of the one who entrusted Fleon-chan to me, she won’t be performing in the circus, I say. But with Fleon-chan’s power, everyone should be able to undergo a Class Up that grants the ability to fly, indeed.”
“Oh, I see—”
“Then I wanna try flying—”
Given how likely it was that Filo-tan, too, would want to fly through the sky, I figured it’d be good to have Fleon-chan lend her assistance for that.
“So the promise that she wouldn’t perform in the circus is indeed being kept.”
“And since the other kids can fly, there’s no issue with that, I suppose.”
“Well… there are bird-type demi-humans and others with the ability to hover or fly, so an aerial trapeze act wouldn’t draw all that much attention on its own.”
“There are dragons and griffins in the ferocious-beast category who can fly too, so… if anything, it’ll probably end up being more about showing people her flying in her Filolial form.”
Everyone went on analyzing things like that, indeed. Fleon-chan landed with a light tap and bowed.
“Looking forward to working with you all from now on!”
And then Fleon-chan began humming the hero song I’d taught her, indeed. A rousing, upbeat tune that burned with passion, I say!
